subject: Post-call: NovusHealth inference economics & pilot hypothesis
messages:
From: Asha Patel <asha.patel@novushealth.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Reddy <samir.reddy@novushealth.com>
Date: 2026-05-30T15:12:23-07:00
Subject: Discovery: Inference cost pressure & latency constraints

Thanks for the sync earlier — appreciate the straightforward discussion. High-level recap from our side and a few clarifying items so we can move to a technical deep-dive: 

Pain points we reiterated on the call:
- Token/unit economics have tripled in the last 6 months as our usage scales (esp. generation-heavy flows).
- We currently run self-hosted endpoints (K8s + Triton wrapper) but are seeing poor utilization and inconsistent p99 latency.
- No prefix caching in place; batching occasionally causes tail latency spikes for interactive users.

Current stack / workload notes I promised to share: 
- Models: mixture of 13B instruction-tuned and some heavier 70B for complex summarization (mostly on-demand).
- Typical sequence lengths: 128 tokens for chat, 512 tokens for summarization.
- Traffic: ~45 RPS average across peak region (US-East), 200k tokens/sec at peak bursts (spiky).
- Latency target: p95 < 120ms, p99 ideally < 350ms for chat flows.

Success criteria for a pilot we care about:
1) Reduce per-token cost by ~40–60% (we're aiming for < $0.015 per 1k tokens overall).
2) Meet p95 / p99 latency targets for interactive experiences.
3) No regressions in output quality (we'll provide 50 sample prompts for eval).
4) Minimal operational overhead / clear rollback plan.

Open to ideas on quantization (we can try INT8/INT4 if quality holds) and batching/caching if it doesn't hurt latency.

Next steps we want from Redwood:
- A short "ask list" of telemetry and logs you need (token distribution, request traces, current batching config).
- A draft mutual action plan (timeline + success metrics) to share with procurement.
- Suggested pilot configuration (instance size, expected throughput, and estimated cost range).

Thanks — I can get you the token-distribution sample and a small eval set by EOD tomorrow.

—Asha
Asha Patel
Director of AI Platforms | NovusHealth

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Asha Patel <asha.patel@novushealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-30T16:03:10-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery: Inference cost pressure & latency constraints
Attachments: redwood-inference-econ-asklist.pdf (application/pdf); cost_model_template.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

Great to meet you both — thanks for the clear summary, Asha. Short reply with what we'll do next and a couple clarifying asks.

Summary of what we heard (confirming):
- Primary goal: immediate reduction in per-token unit cost while keeping interactive latency tight.
- Constraints: some heavy 70B workloads that can't be aggressively quantized without checks; regulatory needs around data residency.

How Redwood would approach a scoped pilot (high level):
1) Instrumentation + telemetry pull: we'll need 7 days of token distribution + request/response traces (send the CSV you mentioned).
2) Quick model profiling: run perf profiles on your 13B/70B variants to see quantization tolerance and cost/latency tradeoffs.
3) Pilot config options: a) Dedicated pool with optimized batching + prefix (KV) caching tuned for your 128/512 distributions; b) Hybrid routing for heavy 70B queries to a fall-back lower-cost variant.
4) Success metrics: match your cost target OR demonstrate clear roadmap to get there in 4 weeks with expected % gains.

Attached: redwood-inference-econ-asklist.pdf (short checklist of exact telemetry + sample curl traces) and a cost_model_template.xlsx you can drop your numbers into.

A few clarifying asks for your team before the technical deep-dive: 
- Can you share sample request-level traces (anonymized) for 48-hours?
- Do you have a strict p99 SLA now, or is it an internal goal?
- Which region(s) must remain in-scope for the pilot (we noted US-East but confirm if US-West / EU needed).

I'm available Thu/Fri morning PST for a 60-min technical deep-dive (Marcus and I will bring an infra engineer). Proposed slots: Thu 10:00 or Fri 09:00. Which works?

Thanks — I'll slot time once I hear back and prep the MAP draft.

—Diego
Diego Fernandez
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-31T09:10:05-07:00
Subject: Internal: Proposed pilot/MAP outline for NovusHealth
Attachments: novus-MAP-draft.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)

Diego — quick internal note after the call. Draft pilot we should propose: 
- 4-week pilot (2-week profiling + 2-week live traffic shadowing + 1-week optional cutover).
- Target fleet: 4 x A100-class for 13B + 2 x H100-style nodes for 70B fallbacks (we'll size more precisely after profiling).
- Config: continuous batching with adaptive max_batch and prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts; conservative INT8 quantization on 13B, hold off on 70B INT4 until eval passes.
- Acceptance criteria: cost delta >= 40% on tokens OR absolute cost per 1k < $0.015, p95 < 120ms in shadowing, no model quality regressions on the provided eval set.

I'll attach a one-page MAP and hand it to Diego to send to Asha/procurement. If they can provide the token CSV and 48h traces today, we can get profiling started tomorrow.

—Marcus
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
